rows.cause: The .sfd gives 'HheadDescent: -16' with 'HheadDOffset: 1', which is an OFFSET, not a value. FontForge's sethhead (tottf.c:2841-2880 at cd438ca99d76) builds the base from int ymin, which is C truncation of the true curve minimum from SplineCharLayerFindBounds. It then widens that to head.yMin. Glyph J's true minimum is -497.5805, which truncates to -497, so FontForge wrote -497-16=-513. babelfont f725e6a (resolve_offset_metrics) uses round(-497.58)=-498 instead and gets -514.

rows.cause: The .sfd gives 'OS2WinDescent: 16' with 'OS2WinDOffset: 1', which is an offset. FontForge's WinBB (tottf.c:3269-3289) uses base -head.yMin. head.yMin is floor(SplineSetQuickBounds) of the exported contours, and before fontforge ee15007274e9 (2014-09-16) QuickBounds counts only ON-CURVE points, including the implied on-curve points a quadratic .sfd writes with flag 128. J's lowest on-curve point is implied at -495.5, which floors to -496, so FontForge wrote 496+16=512. babelfont uses -round(true min)=498 and gets 514.

rows.cause: The release was exported by a FontForge older than commit 4d34d21ef866 (2012-05-14, Khaled Hosny's patch 'it was dividing by the wrong value'). When no top is flat, the old SFStandardHeight (splinefont.c:1702-1706 at cd438ca99d76) does 'test += curves[i].pos; tot += curves[i].cnt;': it adds up the DISTINCT tops and divides by the number of GLYPHS. None of the A-Z tops is flat and I and J share 1503.094, so the result is 36635.1/26 = 1409.04, truncated to 1409. The oracle ports FontForge master, which divides by the distinct count (25) and gets 1465.40 -> 1465.

proposed_converter_changes.description: Offset-mode vertical metrics: use FontForge's exporter bases (babelfont fontforge.rs resolve_offset_metrics, and its inverse offsetmetrics.rs compute_offset_delta). (1) Win base = FontForge's head bbox: per glyph, floor(min)/ceil(max) of the ON-CURVE points of the exported contours, counting implied quadratic on-curve points (flag 128) and resolved references. Off-curve points count only for an exporter from fontforge ee15007274e9 (2014-09-16) or later. winDescent = -head.yMin + offset, winAscent = head.yMax + offset. (2) hhea base = C truncation toward zero of the true curve bounds (SplineCharLayerFindBounds), widened to that head bbox. Today babelfont applies round() of the true bounds to both. Quirk to reproduce: FontForge <= 2012 decides the hhea DESCENDER mode from hheadascent_add (tottf.c:2876); master uses hheaddescent_add. Cubic sources are untested: FontForge measures its own quadratic approximation (SSttfApprox), and every offset-mode style in families.tsv is quadratic.
proposed_converter_changes.evidence: vmetrics_probe.py gives win 512 and hhea -513 under the FontForge <= 2014 rule, equal to the release; babelfont gives 514/-514. vmetrics_sweep.py over families.tsv (60 offset-mode metrics in 15 styles): FontForge rule 41 matches, babelfont 39; the only difference is these 2 rows, with no regressions. Scratch stand-in with absolute values: 7 -> 5 rows (runs/02-proxy-vmetrics). The quoted code is in ff-2010-excerpts.txt.

proposed_converter_changes.description: x-height/cap-height for exporters before 2012-05-14: give fontforge_standard_height.rs (ca43adc, another person's work) a switch. When no top is flat, the curve mean then divides by the GLYPH count (sum of counts) instead of the number of distinct heights, reproducing FontForge before 4d34d21ef866. The flag is chosen per release, the same way baseline.sh already asks the release: turn it on when the release's FFTM FFTimeStamp is before 2012-05-14.
proposed_converter_changes.evidence: heights_pre2012_probe.py: 31 of 38 releases reproduced vs 25 of 38 with the master rule. The six added styles all have FFTM builds from 2010-04-29 or 2011-02-22, and none is lost. PatrickHand (FFTM 2012-09-06, after the fix) is unaffected. For this style: cap height 1409 (release 1409) vs 1465; x-height 1095 under both.

proposed_converter_changes.description: FontForge's shared script list: when the source has lookups in only one of GSUB and GPOS, emit the other table with the same scripts and languages (empty default LangSys) and 0 features / 0 lookups, as FontForge's SFScriptsInLookups + dumpg___info did. The .glyphs format and FEA cannot express this, so babelfont alone cannot do it. It needs a fontc option or a gftools-builder3 post-compile step in the recipe, keyed to FontForge-exported releases.
proposed_converter_changes.evidence: empty_gpos_probe.py adds this shell to our build: the 3 GPOS rows close, no other row opens, and horizontal HarfBuzz shaping goes from 648 differing runs to 0 of the ltr/rtl share of 25008. fea_empty_feature_test.sh shows an empty 'feature kern {} kern;' makes fontc 1.0.0 emit no GPOS. In families.tsv, 23 releases carry FontForge's shell (19 with an empty GSUB, 4 with an empty GPOS). Only this one blocks, because it is the only style with combining marks; the table_gate _nothing_to_position guard passes the rest.

edit_verdicts.commit_subject: (toolchain) emit FontForge's shared-script empty GPOS shell
edit_verdicts.reason: The cause is right: SFScriptsInLookups deliberately ignores gpos, 'for Uniscribe'. The rule as written is wrong on languages: SFLangsInScript (lookups.c:375-425) is per table, so a script with no lookups in a table gets only a dummy DEFAULT_LANG (dflt). Scripts are the UNION of both tables and go into both tables even when both have lookups. Their 'same scripts and languages' rule, and their probe copying GSUB LangSysRecords, would over-emit languages; this font is unaffected because it has only dflt. It cannot be done in babelfont or FEA: a kern block holding only script/language statements also yields no GPOS from fontc 1.0.0 (my runs/05). It deliberately re-disables HarfBuzz fallback mark positioning, which is Felipe's decision.

edit_verdicts.commit_subject: (naming) UnifrakturMaguntia-Book.ttf -> UnifrakturMaguntia-Regular.ttf as a METADATA.pb files-mapping matter
edit_verdicts.reason: The FontForge side is correct: 2010 _GetModifiers falls back to 'Weight: Book' for nameID 2. But 'not a source edit, just mapping' understates it. babelfont (fontforge.rs ~L985) names the master 'Regular' from TTFWeight 400 and never uses the stated Weight (it is parked as postscript_weight_name). Result: nameID 2 Book->Regular, nameID 4 gains ' Regular', and PostScript name UnifrakturMaguntia -> UnifrakturMaguntia-Regular. The gate accepts this, but it is a silent converter normalisation. METADATA.pb filename/post_script_name/full_name must follow and the PR must disclose it. An .sfd 'Weight: Regular' edit would be documentary only.

classification_objections: GPOS.script_list/feature_list/lookup_list as 'converter-fidelity': the cause is accepted, but these rows cannot be closed by the converter (babelfont), the .glyphs format or FEA. They are toolchain (fontc or builder3 post-step) fidelity, and the mechanism is undecided, so they stay open until someone picks one. Blocking is correct (not gate-arbitration): without the shell, 1317 of 1386 ltr base+mark texts shape differently.
missed: --add-legacy-duplicate-cmap misfires for this style. The .sfd itself maps U+00A0 to space (AltUni2) and has its own uni00AD, so the harness's test (release carries 00A0 and 00AD) says yes, and the flag then adds U+02C9->macron and U+2219->periodcentered, which the release does not map. table_gate cmap_blocking accepts gained codepoints and prints nothing. With DROP_FLAGS=--add-legacy-duplicate-cmap the cmap is identical to the release (247/247) and the same 7 rows remain. For this style it is not a fidelity flag; the harness should test for the synthesised duplicates themselves.

OS/2.fs_selection is 64 in the release and 192 in ours, and the gate accepts it wholesale. The .sfd states OS2_UseTypoMetrics 1 with OS2Version 3, and FontForge 2010 sets bit 7 only for version>=4 (tottf.c:3331-3337). It changes the HarfBuzz vertical advance (2121 vs 2120) and line spacing in apps that honour the bit. Their unresolved note blames the vertical residue only on glyf header bboxes, but their own nobit7 control shows bit 7 accounts for part of it (ttb 6225 -> 5232 runs).

Their claim 'only this one blocks because it is the only style with combining marks' is false as stated: Monoton (4), Smythe (2), Tuffy-Bold/BoldItalic (19) and UnifrakturCook-Bold (9) also have marks, but their shell is an empty GSUB. Correct statement: it is the only one of the 4 empty-GPOS releases (Kristi, Lekton-Bold, Lekton-Regular, UnifrakturMaguntia-Book) with marks. The 19/4 census itself is confirmed.

Their provenance claim names cd438ca99d76 as the exporter. The exact build is the FontForge 20100501 release (libffstamp LibFF_ModTime == FFTM FFTimeStamp 1272512607). The relevant files are byte-identical to cd438, so the conclusions stand.

verification.overall: The findings hold up. Every figure in the 7 rows reproduces from the unmodified source: rows go 7 -> 5 -> 3 -> 0 with the stand-ins plus a GPOS graft. My own port of the exact exporter source (the FontForge 20100501 tarball, whose stamp equals FFTM) reproduces each value. All 7 classifications are sound in cause. The GPOS rows are toolchain fidelity rather than babelfont, and remain open until a mechanism is chosen. Proposal verdicts: keep both converter rules (vmetrics, pre-2012 heights); revise the GPOS-shell rule (languages are per table, with a dummy dflt only; scripts are the union); reframe the Book->Regular naming as a disclosed silent converter normalisation rather than a pure METADATA mapping. Three non-blocking misses: the duplicate-cmap flag adds 2 codepoints the release lacks; USE_TYPO_METRICS is set where FontForge 2010 did not set it; and the marks-only-here claim is imprecise.
